newsitem.title: USA: US aluminum premiums wobble a touch, alloy firmer.
newsitem.headline: US aluminum premiums wobble a touch, alloy firmer.

text.p: Physical business in the U.S. aluminum market was quiet this week, but no less than 21 companies jostled for 10,000 short tons of surplus Stockpile metal, dealers said.

"This time the bids for Stockpile metal were really quite aggressive," a physical merchant said. "Allowing for a penny freight to ship it out of the DLA (Stockpile), that metal probably went close to 4.00 cents a lb on a delivered basis."
Stockpile was due to announce the awards for aluminum soon, but trader Glencore was expected to win a large share.
Stockpile aluminum has not yet disrupted the U.S. physical market in any major way, market participants said.
"I think people are using it against some of their chain metal they are late on," a producer official said. "Some people say they have not received shipments from February yet on releases."
U.S. spot aluminum premiums were quoted at 4.25 to 4.75 cents per lb over LME cash, delivered to consumer. Some merchants noted they could buy chain metal at 4.00 cents.
"The physical side is still extremely quiet, but premiums are pretty well supported," a New York trader said.
Downward pressure on alloy appears to have eased, for the moment at least, smelter officials said.
The benchmark A380 LME deliverable alloy was slightly higher at 74.00 to 75.00 cents a lb, up about a cent from the nadir of the past month.
Smelters have been squeezed more than usual in recent weeks because of firm scrap prices amid weakening alloy tags. Scrap tags edged up slightly again this week.
"The alloy market is starting to come back a little bit. We are now not quoting under 75.00 to 76.00 cents," an East Coast smelter official said.
But another alloys sales executive said most of the contractual business for July has been done and it was too early in the month for spot sales.
"August is a mystery but I would expect alloy prices to go lower because business will slow down. We are starting to see it," the sales executive said.
The sector was looking for clues in the latest car sales figures. Alloy is used for making components.
Chrysler's June vehicle sales in the U.S. fell 4 percent, and other carmakers were offering low interest sales deals in an attempt to boost flagging shipments, alloy industry officials noted.
